page.name: Routing and automatic failover
page.metaTitle: Routing and automatic failover for SMS
page.metaDescription: Send across more than one connected SMS account, with automatic failover when one stops accepting traffic.
page.lede: One provider account is a single point of failure that you cannot see failing until customers tell you. Routing across several accounts turns that into a failover you configure once.

sections.h: Built end to end on the SMS channel
p: Automatic failover between connected accounts ships on the SMS channel — the channel where provider-side failures are the ones that hurt: a number throttled, an account suspended, a route that quietly stops accepting traffic. That path is built end to end, which is why this is where the feature lives.

Failover changes which provider carries a message. The destination carrier still decides whether it lands, and a route that is wrong on every account still has to be fixed at the source — because there would be nowhere left to route to.
bullets: A single send can be carried by any of your connected SMS accounts
An account that stops accepting traffic is taken out of the route
A problem that affects every account surfaces instead of hiding behind a retry

sections.h: How it works together with pacing
p: Failover and pacing solve different problems: pacing keeps you under the limit a provider applies per number, failover keeps traffic moving when an account stops working. Configure both, and neither failure mode is left open.

faq.q: Is failover available for email or WhatsApp?
faq.a: Failover across connected accounts ships on the SMS channel today. Email and WhatsApp carry their own provider-side limits and are handled separately.
No. It changes the provider carrying the message. Delivery still depends on the destination network accepting it.

faq.q: What decides the order accounts are tried in?
faq.a: Routing works across the accounts you have connected for that channel. The mechanics and their limits are described in the routing guide rather than restated here.
